newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prods fall as traders dismiss fire.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prods fall as traders dismiss fire.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products fell Friday after traders shrugged off a fire at a small Los Angeles gasoline unit.
The unit, a 25,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker, was hit by a fire late Thursday but sustained no structural damage, according to a Tosco offficial. It's return date was unknown.
Wholesale prices were unchanged early, the support gave way after traders determined the unit's lost capacity was slight compared to rising supplies.
"The fire did nothing....It's a smaller gasoline unit than an FCC," said one broker.
He referred to a fluid catalytic cracker, which makes most of a refinery's gasoline.
Gasoline on hand at West Coast refineries was up 98,000 barrels last week as most refineries resumed full production following spring maintenance.
Overall, CARB gasoline in Los Angeles fell two cents from Thursday, and 13.50 cents from March 25 -- a 15.7 percent dive in just over a week.
Traders said L.A. CARB gasoline was talked 72 to 74 cents a gallon Friday, while San Francisco grade was 65/66 cents, also two cents lower.
